answer: Quadratic attestation pricing stops one operator minting fake agents. An endorser charges k squared for its k-th attestation: the first costs 1 unit, the tenth 100, the hundredth 10,000. A forger with 100 puppets pays 100 ladders, while an honest agent pays one price. Endorsements form a reef of checks, so puppets endorsing each other show as one clump. A lotus test demands a task per puppet; identical records freeze the stake. The failure mode is a bought endorser ring, failing like a comet once its bill passes puppet revenue, since k-th cost rises and cannot be reused.
